## Reading Data

We continue using the Seoul Bike Sharing dataset from HW9. We fit and compare models using tidymodels.

```{r}
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(lubridate)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidymodels)
library(baguette)
library(ranger)
library(rpart.plot)

bike_data <- read_csv(
  "https://www4.stat.ncsu.edu/~online/datasets/SeoulBikeData.csv",
  locale = locale(encoding = "latin1")
)

head(bike_data)
dim(bike_data)
```

### EDA

We repeat the data checks and preparation from HW9.

#### Checking Missing Values

```{r}
colSums(is.na(bike_data))
```

#### Checking Variable Types and Values

```{r}
str(bike_data)

bike_data |>
  select(where(is.numeric)) |>
  summary()

unique(bike_data$Seasons)
unique(bike_data$Holiday)
unique(bike_data$`Functioning Day`)
```

#### Cleaning the Data

We rename the columns, convert dates and change categorical variables to factors.

```{r}
bike <- bike_data

names(bike) <- c(
  "date", "rented_count", "hour", "temp",
  "humidity", "wind_speed", "visibility",
  "dew_point_temp", "solar_radiation",
  "rainfall", "snowfall", "seasons",
  "holiday", "functioning_day"
)

bike <- bike |>
  mutate(date = dmy(date)) |>
  mutate(
    across(
      c(seasons, holiday, functioning_day),
      as.factor
    )
  )

head(bike)
```

```{r}
bike |>

    sd_bikes = sd(rented_count),

bike |>

bike |>

  summarize(
    mean_bikes = mean(rented_count),
    median_bikes = median(rented_count),
    sd_bikes = sd(rented_count),
    min_bikes = min(rented_count),
    max_bikes = max(rented_count),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

bike |>
  group_by(functioning_day) |>
  summarize(
    mean_bikes = mean(rented_count),
    median_bikes = median(rented_count),
    sd_bikes = sd(rented_count),
    min_bikes = min(rented_count),
    max_bikes = max(rented_count),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

#### Removing Non-Functioning Hours

We remove observations when the rental system was not operating.

```{r}
bike <- bike |>
  filter(functioning_day == "Yes")

dim(bike)
```

#### Creating Daily Data

We sum bike rentals, rainfall and snowfall for each day. We average the other weather variables.

```{r}
daily <- bike |>
  group_by(date, seasons, holiday) |>
  summarise(
    rented_count = sum(rented_count),
    rainfall = sum(rainfall),
    snowfall = sum(snowfall),
    temp = mean(temp),
    humidity = mean(humidity),
    wind_speed = mean(wind_speed),
    visibility = mean(visibility),
    dew_point_temp = mean(dew_point_temp),
    solar_radiation = mean(solar_radiation),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

daily
dim(daily)
```

#### Daily Summary Statistics

```{r}
summary(daily)

daily |>
  group_by(seasons) |>
  summarize(
    mean_bikes = mean(rented_count),
    median_bikes = median(rented_count),
    sd_bikes = sd(rented_count),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

daily |>
  group_by(holiday) |>
  summarize(
    mean_bikes = mean(rented_count),
    median_bikes = median(rented_count),
    sd_bikes = sd(rented_count),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

We calculate the mean daily rentals for each combination before drawing the heatmap.

Temperature has a strong positive correlation with daily bike rentals. Solar radiation also has a strong positive relationship with rentals.

## Split the Data

We use a 75/25 split stratified by seasons. We then create 10 cross-validation folds from the training set.

```{r}
set.seed(558)

bike_split <- initial_split(
  daily,
  prop = 0.75,
  strata = seasons
)

bike_train <- training(bike_split)
bike_test <- testing(bike_split)

bike_folds <- vfold_cv(bike_train, v = 10)

bike_split
bike_folds
```

## Fitting MLR Models

### Recipes

#### Recipe 1

We create a weekday/weekend factor from the date. We give the original date an ID role, standardize numeric predictors and create dummy variables.

```{r}
MLR_recipe1 <- recipe(
  rented_count ~ .,
  data = bike_train
) |>
  update_role(date, new_role = "id") |>
  step_date(date, features = "dow") |>
  step_mutate(
    day_type = factor(
      if_else(
        date_dow %in% c("Sat", "Sun"),
        "weekend",
        "weekday"
      )
    )
  ) |>
  step_rm(date_dow) |>
  step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors()) |>
  step_dummy(seasons, holiday, day_type)

MLR_recipe1
```

#### Recipe 2

We add interactions between seasons and holiday, seasons and temperature plus temperature and rainfall.

```{r}
MLR_recipe2 <- recipe(
  rented_count ~ .,
  data = bike_train
) |>
  update_role(date, new_role = "id") |>
  step_date(date, features = "dow") |>
  step_mutate(
    day_type = factor(
      if_else(
        date_dow %in% c("Sat", "Sun"),
        "weekend",
        "weekday"
      )
    )
  ) |>
  step_rm(date_dow) |>
  step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors()) |>
  step_dummy(seasons, holiday, day_type) |>
  step_interact(
    ~ starts_with("seasons"):starts_with("holiday") +
      starts_with("seasons"):temp +
      temp:rainfall
  )

MLR_recipe2
```

#### Recipe 3

We keep the interactions and add squared terms for standardized temperature and humidity.

```{r}
MLR_recipe3 <- recipe(
  rented_count ~ .,
  data = bike_train
) |>
  update_role(date, new_role = "id") |>
  step_date(date, features = "dow") |>
  step_mutate(
    day_type = factor(
      if_else(
        date_dow %in% c("Sat", "Sun"),
        "weekend",
        "weekday"
      )
    )
  ) |>
  step_rm(date_dow) |>
  step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors()) |>
  step_dummy(seasons, holiday, day_type) |>
  step_interact(
    ~ starts_with("seasons"):starts_with("holiday") +
      starts_with("seasons"):temp +
      temp:rainfall
  ) |>
  step_mutate(
    tetmp_sq = temp^2,
    humidity_sq = humidity^2
  )

MLR_recipe3
```

### Fit via 10-Fold CV

We use the lm engine for all three recipes.

```{r}
MLR_spec <- linear_reg() |>
  set_engine("lm")

MLR_workflow1 <- workflow() |>
  add_recipe(MLR_recipe1) |>
  add_model(MLR_spec)

MLR_workflow2 <- workflow() |>
  add_recipe(MLR_recipe2) |>
  add_model(MLR_spec)

MLR_workflow3 <- workflow() |>
  add_recipe(MLR_recipe3) |>
  add_model(MLR_spec)

MLR_workflows <- list(
  recipe1 = MLR_workflow1,
  recipe2 = MLR_workflow2,
  recipe3 = MLR_workflow3
)

MLR_results <- bind_rows(
  fit_resamples(MLR_workflow1, bike_folds) |>
    collect_metrics() |>
    mutate(model = "recipe1"),

  fit_resamples(MLR_workflow2, bike_folds) |>
    collect_metrics() |>
    mutate(model = "recipe2"),

  fit_resamples(MLR_workflow3, bike_folds) |>
    collect_metrics() |>
    mutate(model = "recipe3")
)

MLR_results |>
  filter(.metric == "rmse") |>
  select(model, mean, std_err) |>
  knitr::kable(
    digits = 2,
    caption = "MLR Cross-Validation RMSE"
  )
```

We choose the recipe with the lowest mean cross-validation RMSE.

```{r}
MLR_best_workflow <- MLR_results |>
  filter(.metric == "rmse") |>
  arrange(mean) |>
  slice(1)

MLR_best_workflow

last_mlr <- last_fit(
  MLR_workflows[[MLR_best_workflow$model]],
  bike_split,
  metrics = metric_set(
    yardstick::rmse,
    yardstick::mae
  )
)

collect_metrics(last_mlr)
```

The selected recipe is **`r MLR_best_workflow$model[[1]]`**. Its mean cross-validation RMSE is **`r round(MLR_best_workflow$mean[[1]], 2)`**.

## Fitting Other Models

We use the first MLR recipe for all three tree-based models. We tune each model using the training folds.

### Regression Tree

We tune cost complexity and tree depth.

```{r}
tree_spec <- decision_tree(
  cost_complexity = tune(),
  tree_depth = tune()
) |>
  set_engine("rpart") |>
  set_mode("regression")

tree_workflow <- workflow() |>
  add_recipe(MLR_recipe1) |>
  add_model(tree_spec)

tree_grid <- tree_workflow |>
  tune_grid(
    resamples = bike_folds,
    grid = grid_regular(
      cost_complexity(),
      tree_depth(),
      levels = 5
    )
  )

tree_best_params <- tree_grid |>
  select_best(metric = "rmse")

tree_best_params

tree_final_workflow <- tree_workflow |>
  finalize_workflow(tree_best_params)

tree_final_fit <- tree_final_workflow |>
  fit(bike_train)
```

### Bagged Tree

We combine 25 trees and tune cost complexity and tree depth.

```{r}
bag_spec <- bag_tree(
  cost_complexity = tune(),
  tree_depth = tune()
) |>
  set_engine("rpart", times = 25) |>
  set_mode("regression")

bag_workflow <- workflow() |>
  add_recipe(MLR_recipe1) |>
  add_model(bag_spec)

bag_grid <- bag_workflow |>
  tune_grid(
    resamples = bike_folds,
    grid = grid_regular(
      cost_complexity(),
      tree_depth(),
      levels = 3
    )
  )

bag_best_params <- bag_grid |>
  select_best(metric = "rmse")

bag_best_params

bag_final_workflow <- bag_workflow |>
  finalize_workflow(bag_best_params)

bag_final_fit <- bag_final_workflow |>
  fit(bike_train)
```

### Random Forest

We use 500 trees and tune mtry and min_n. We enable impurity importance for the variable importance plot.

```{r}
rf_spec <- rand_forest(
  mtry = tune(),
  min_n = tune(),
  trees = 500
) |>
  set_engine("ranger", importance = "impurity") |>
  set_mode("regression")

rf_workflow <- workflow() |>
  add_recipe(MLR_recipe1) |>
  add_model(rf_spec)

rf_grid <- rf_workflow |>
  tune_grid(
    resamples = bike_folds,
    grid = grid_regular(
      mtry(range = c(2, 10)),
      min_n(range = c(2, 10)),
      levels = 3
    )
  )

rf_best_params <- rf_grid |>
  select_best(metric = "rmse")

rf_best_params

rf_final_workflow <- rf_workflow |>
  finalize_workflow(rf_best_params)

rf_final_fit <- rf_final_workflow |>
  fit(bike_train)
```

## Compare on the Test Set

We fit each selected workflow on the full training set and evaluate it on the same test set. Lower RMSE and MAE mean smaller prediction errors.

```{r}
last_tree <- last_fit(
  tree_final_workflow,
  bike_split,
  metrics = metric_set(
    yardstick::rmse,
    yardstick::mae
  )
)

last_bag <- last_fit(
  bag_final_workflow,
  bike_split,
  metrics = metric_set(
    yardstick::rmse,
    yardstick::mae
  )
)

last_rf <- last_fit(
  rf_final_workflow,
  bike_split,
  metrics = metric_set(
    yardstick::rmse,
    yardstick::mae
  )
)

test_results <- bind_rows(
  collect_metrics(last_mlr) |>
    mutate(model = "MLR"),

  collect_metrics(last_tree) |>
    mutate(model = "Regression Tree"),

  collect_metrics(last_bag) |>
    mutate(model = "Bagged Tree"),

  collect_metrics(last_rf) |>
    mutate(model = "Random Forest")
)

rmse_table <- test_results |>
  filter(.metric == "rmse") |>
  select(model, rmse = .estimate) |>
  arrange(rmse)

rmse_table |>
  knitr::kable(
    digits = 2,
    caption = "Test RMSE"
  )

mae_table <- test_results |>
  filter(.metric == "mae") |>
  select(model, mae = .estimate) |>
  arrange(mae)

mae_table |>
  knitr::kable(
    digits = 2,
    caption = "Test MAE"
  )
```


### Regression Tree Model

```{r}

tree_final_fit |>

    roundint = FALSE,
    main = "Final Regression Tree"

```

### Bagged Tree Variable Importance

We plot the importance scores from the fitted bagged trees.

```{r}
bag_importance <- bag_final_fit |>
  extract_fit_engine() |>
  baguette::var_imp()

bag_importance |>
  arrange(desc(value)) |>
  knitr::kable(
    digits = 2,
    caption = "Bagged Tree Variable Importance"
  )

ggplot(
  bag_importance,
  aes(x = reorder(term, value), y = value)
) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Bagged Tree Variable Importance",
    x = "Predictor",
    y = "Importance"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

### Random Forest Variable Importance

We extract the importance scores from the ranger model and plot them.

```{r}
rf_engine <- rf_final_fit |>
  extract_fit_engine()

rf_importance <- tibble(
  term = names(rf_engine$variable.importance),
  value = as.numeric(rf_engine$variable.importance)
)

rf_importance |>
  arrange(desc(value)) |>
  knitr::kable(
    digits = 2,
    caption = "Random Forest Variable Importance"
  )

ggplot(
  rf_importance,
  aes(x = reorder(term, value), y = value)
) +
  geom_col(fill = "darkgreen") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Random Forest Variable Importance",
    x = "Predictor",
    y = "Impurity Importance"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Overall Best Model - Refit on Entire Data Set

We select the model with the lowest test RMSE and refit it using all daily observations.

```{r}
rmse_table
mae_table

best_overall <- rmse_table$model[1]
best_overall

if (best_overall == "MLR") {
  overall_best_workflow <-
    MLR_workflows[[MLR_best_workflow$model]]
} else if (best_overall == "Regression Tree") {
  overall_best_workflow <- tree_final_workflow
} else if (best_overall == "Bagged Tree") {
  overall_best_workflow <- bag_final_workflow
} else {
  overall_best_workflow <- rf_final_workflow
}

overall_best_fit <- overall_best_workflow |>
  fit(daily)

overall_best_fit
```

## Conclusion

The best MLR recipe based on cross-validation was **`r MLR_best_workflow$model[[1]]`**.

The **`r best_overall`** model had the lowest test RMSE of **`r round(rmse_table$rmse[[1]], 2)`**. Its test MAE was **`r round(mae_table$mae[match(best_overall, mae_table$model)], 2)`**.

We refitted this model using all **`r nrow(daily)`** daily observations.
